parts.title: A year with the monkeys
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I told my friends that I was going to spend a year in the rainforest, most of them thought I was mad. I am a scientist, and I wanted to study a small group of monkeys in the north of Peru. I arrived in January with two big bags and a lot of excitement.

The first month was the hardest. It rained almost every afternoon, and my clothes never dried. I slept in a small hut with a tin roof, and the noise of the rain was so loud that I could not hear myself think. I also had to learn to walk quietly, because the monkeys ran away if they heard me coming.

Slowly, things became easier. A local guide called Mateo taught me which plants were safe to touch and how to find my way using the sun and the sounds of the river. After three months, the monkeys stopped hiding. One young monkey even sat on a branch next to my notebook and watched me write.

Now I am back at home, and I miss the forest every day. I have learned that nature is much stronger than people think, but it needs our help. My plan is to go back next year and to bring some students with me.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer's friends think she was mad?
options: She chose to live in the forest for a year
She took far too many bags on her journey
She went to Peru with no plan at all
She had never travelled by plane or by boat
questions.explanation: Her friends thought she was mad when she said she would spend a year in the rainforest.

questions.prompt: What made the first month difficult?
options: The long walk to the nearest town
The animals made noises all night
The weak signal for her mobile phone in the hut
The afternoon rain and the wet clothes
questions.explanation: It rained almost every afternoon, and her clothes never dried.

questions.prompt: Why did she learn to walk quietly?
options: Her notebook made too much noise at night
The monkeys ran off when they heard her
The guide had asked her to do so
The ground was covered in wet leaves
questions.explanation: The monkeys ran away if they heard her coming.

questions.prompt: What did Mateo teach her?
options: How to take good photos of monkeys
How to build a safe wooden hut quickly
How to find her way in the forest
Which animals were safe to touch
questions.explanation: He showed her how to find her way using the sun and the sounds of the river.

questions.prompt: What does the writer plan to do next year?
options: Go back and take students along
Visit a different country with her friends
Write a book about her time
Study a different kind of animal
questions.explanation: She plans to go back next year and bring some students with her.

parts.title: A visit to the world's biggest rainforest
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
The Amazon is the largest rainforest on Earth. It covers parts of nine countries, and it is so big that you could fit most of Europe inside it. [1] Scientists believe that about one in ten of all the animals and plants in the world live there.

A trip to the Amazon usually begins in a river town. [2] From there, small boats carry visitors deep into the forest, where there are no roads at all.

The weather is hot and wet all year, and the air feels like a warm bath. [3] Visitors are told to pack light clothes that dry fast and a good raincoat.

In the evening, the forest becomes noisy. [4] Guides say that it is the best time to see frogs, insects and even small cats.

Sadly, every year large areas of forest are cut down for farms. [5] Many visitors leave with a strong wish to protect this special place.
sentences: This means there are more kinds of life here than almost anywhere else.
Several million people live in the Amazon, many of them in cities.
The sounds of thousands of creatures fill the dark.
The roads there were built over fifty years ago.
Because of this, many animals are losing their homes.
That is why the river is brown for most of the year.
Tourists can buy food, water and tickets at the busy market there.
It can rain for an hour and then the sun comes out again.

gaps.explanation: The extra sentence about more kinds of life follows the size of the forest and leads to the scientists' figure.
The market in the river town explains where visitors get supplies before the boats leave.
Rain followed by sun explains why light, fast-drying clothes and a raincoat are needed.
The sounds of creatures in the dark explain why the evening is noisy.
Cutting down forests for farms explains why animals lose their homes.

parts.title: An email from a student in Brazil
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Hi Jess, I have been in Brazil for a week now and it is amazing! Yesterday we [1] a boat trip along a river in the forest. The guide [2] us to be quiet, so that we could hear the birds. I saw a green parrot sitting [3] a branch above my head. It is much hotter here than at home, [4] I drink about three litres of water every day. Tomorrow we are going to visit a village, and I am really looking forward [5] meeting the children there. I hope you [6] a great time at school at the moment. Love, Rosa

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: Take a boat trip is the usual phrase, and the verb is in the past simple.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Told + object + to + verb is the correct pattern.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: A bird sits on a branch.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: Drinking a lot of water is the result of the heat, so "so" fits.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: Look forward to + -ing.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: Present continuous for what is happening now at school.

parts.title: Saving the forest
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Many people think that the rainforest is only important for the animals that live there, but it is useful for everyone. The trees give us the air [1] breathe, and they also help to keep the weather stable. Some of the medicines that doctors use [2] made from forest plants. When farmers cut down [3] much forest, the soil can wash away in the rain. Today, [4] are many groups that work to protect the trees. Some of them plant new forests, and others teach children [5] to look after nature. If we all do a little, we [6] make a difference.

gaps.explanation: "The air we breathe" needs a subject pronoun.
Some of the medicines ... are made: plural passive.
"Too much forest" or "so much forest": both express a large amount; "too" is the expected answer.
"There are many groups" introduces the existence of groups.
Teach children how to look after nature.
Can make a difference is the natural modal here.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Marisol, you’re not going into the forest like that, are you? It’s going to pour any moment.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I know. I thought about buying an umbrella from the shop, but they’re big and I’d hit every branch. Anyway, they cost twelve dollars.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What about waiting for the guide? He said he’d bring spare things.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: He’s stuck in town, and I don’t want to lose an hour. But the man at the gate told me they lend coats for the rain, and it’s free. I’ll take one when I sign in.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Good plan. I’ll come with you.

question.prompt: What will the woman do at the gate?
question.explanation: She does not want a big umbrella and will not wait for the late guide; the gate lends coats for the rain, so she will borrow a raincoat.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome aboard. Let me tell you about the day. I know the programme says we will have lunch at the end of the trip, at about four, but that was an old plan, and it was too late for most people. We are going to stop at a village on the river after we have walked for one hour, and the cooks will give us hot rice and fish. The boat leaves at eleven, but we will be back long before that, so you won’t miss it. Please keep your bottles full.

options: At the end of the trip
question.explanation: The programme said the end of the trip, but the plan changed, and the boat leaves at eleven when they are back; lunch is in a village after one hour of walking.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Look, Philomena, a toucan! I thought they lived near the river bank.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: You do see them there, drinking in the morning, and one lazy bird once walked on the forest floor, but that’s unusual. They like the highest branches, where they build nests in holes in old trunks.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: So we’ll rarely see one close.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Not unless you bring binoculars. The guide says that at the tops of the tall trees they have everything: fruit, shade and safety.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Then I’ll take a lot of photos with the zoom.

options: In the tops of the trees
question.explanation: She says toucans drink at the bank and sometimes walk on the floor, but they live in the highest branches of the tall trees.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’m sorry, I’m going to sit down. I don’t understand why the forest feels so hot. The sun is not even out.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Because of the air, I think. It’s full of water, so it feels like a steam room.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Really? I thought it was because of the sun.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: In a clearing, perhaps, but under the trees there’s lots of shade. Even so, the leaves hold the moisture, and it stays close to the ground.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I see. So that’s why my clothes are wet.

question.prompt: Why does the forest feel hot?
options: The sun is very strong all day
The air holds a lot of water
There are no trees to give shade
question.explanation: She believes it is the sun and he mentions the shade; the real reason is that the air is full of water.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Have you seen my torch, Winnifred? We need it for tonight’s walk.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Did you leave it in the hut under the bed? I thought I saw it there on Monday.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I looked there, and I also dug through my rucksack, even the little pockets. It’s nowhere.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Wait. You came in with your hat and your tea last night, and you put things down, didn’t you?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I did! Oh, there it is, right next to the hat, where the tea was. I feel silly.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Don’t worry. Let’s go!

options: Under the bed in the hut
On the table near his hat
question.explanation: It was not under the bed or in the rucksack; he had put it on the table next to his hat.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Hi, Bridie, it’s Tiernan. I’m sitting at the lodge writing a long list of every animal we saw today, with the Latin names. I know you think it’s for you, and I’ll send you pictures later, but not this. The guide asked if he could have a copy for his office, but I need it for school. I’m teaching a class about the rainforest next week, and the children are going to learn all the names. So don’t worry, I’ll send you something nice instead. Speak soon.

question.prompt: Why is the man writing a list?
options: To use it in a lesson
To give it to the guide
To send it to a friend
question.explanation: He says his friend and the guide would like it, but he explains that he is teaching a class next week.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hi, Ludovic, it’s Ondine. I’m at the camp, and I’m writing to say that it’s amazing here. Everybody wants to try the zip wire, and I’ll admit I did think about it. But when I looked down, I changed my mind. Another group stayed in their tents all afternoon and played cards, and I was not interested. There’s a walk high up on bridges between the tree tops, and I booked a place for the morning. That’s what I want to do. You should come, it’s only twenty dollars. Call me later and tell me what you think.

question.prompt: What does the woman want to do?
question.explanation: She thought about the zip wire but changed her mind, and she did not want to stay at the camp; she booked the walk on bridges among the tree tops.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Are you all right, Lochlan? You’ve been quiet since we got in the boat.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Actually, I’m fine. I thought I’d be nervous, because I can’t swim well, but the water’s calm and the life jackets feel safe.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: And what about the animals? We haven’t seen many.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: That’s true, but I don’t mind. The air is fresh, the trees are huge and it’s so peaceful. It’s much better than the city. I’d stay here all day.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Me too. Let’s ask the driver to go slowly.

question.prompt: How does Lochlan feel about the boat trip?
options: Pleased to be on the river
question.explanation: He expected to be nervous but is not, and he does not mind the lack of animals; he enjoys the calm river, so he is pleased to be there.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Gwyneth, my bag has gone. I had it when we got off the boat.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Are you sure it’s not on the boat? I can run back and look.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: The driver left five minutes ago, so that won’t help. I could phone the hotel, but I haven’t been there since breakfast.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Then ask the guide. He saw everybody climb off, and he walks the path every day, so he’d know.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Good point. He’s talking to the cook now. I’ll go and find him.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’ll come with you.

question.prompt: What do Cassius and Gwyneth decide to do about the lost bag?
options: Look for it in the boat
question.explanation: The boat driver has gone and the bag was not left at the hotel, so they decide to ask the guide, who sees everyone.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I heard you took your class into the forest, Thandi. How was it?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Wonderful. I thought the children would run off, but they stayed together and asked questions all day. Preparation was easy, I just made a list.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: So it didn’t take a lot of effort?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Not at all. And what surprised me was the mood. Everybody was smiling, even the shy ones. In class, I have to work hard to get a smile. Out there, they learned and laughed at the same time.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’d like to try it.

question.prompt: What does Thandi think about teaching outdoors?
options: It is harder to keep attention
It is more fun than a classroom
It takes more time to prepare
question.explanation: She expected problems with attention and a lot of preparation, but found neither; the children smiled and laughed, so it was more fun.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: You must be annoyed about the rain, Ewart. We were going to climb the hill today.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Not at all. We can climb tomorrow. Honestly, I’m relieved. It was so hot yesterday that I could hardly breathe.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: But the path will be slippery, won’t it? And the river could flood.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: The guide says it never gets that high. And I’d rather have a wet path than a burning sun. Listen, it’s so much quieter now. Let’s have coffee on the porch.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Okay, you’ve convinced me.

question.prompt: How does Ewart feel about the rain?
options: Glad that it cools the air
Afraid that the path will flood
Angry that it ruins the trip
question.explanation: Saoirse suggests that he is annoyed and mentions flooding, but he is relieved because the rain makes it cooler than the hot day before.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Shall we try that restaurant in town tonight? It’s got good reviews.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: The food looks great, but it’s twenty minutes by taxi. And you know I’m shattered after the walk.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Is it a money problem? The hotel is cheaper.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No, it’s not about that, and I’m sure the town place is open. I just want to sit down, have a hot meal and go to bed early.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: You’re right, I’m not much better. The hotel it is.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Thanks. We’ll go to the town one tomorrow.

question.prompt: Why do they decide to eat in the hotel tonight?
options: It is cheaper than the town
They are too tired to go out
question.explanation: Imelda mentions the price and Thaddeus is sure the town place is open; he says he is shattered, and both are tired, so they stay at the hotel.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Lilibet, I heard that you are signing up for the volunteer programme. Is it because of the free trip?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No, the trip isn’t free, we pay for our food and the bed. And I have plenty of friends already.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Then why?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Last year I saw a young monkey that had lost its home because of a fire. They were saving it, and I felt I had to be a part of it. I want to protect those animals so that my grandchildren can see them.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: That’s a lovely reason. Can I join you?

question.prompt: Why does Lilibet want to become a volunteer?
question.explanation: She says the trip is not free and she has many friends; she saw a young monkey being saved and wants to protect animals.

parts.title: A talk about the Amazon
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: hanne
turns.text: Hello everyone, and thank you for coming. Today I would like to tell you about my favourite place, the Amazon rainforest. Let me start with the river. Many people think that the Nile is the biggest river in the world, and there are some people who say the Amazon is the widest. But in South America, no other river goes as far as this one, so we call it the longest. Because the forest is so thick, there are very few roads, so it is not a good idea to hire a car. Some people use small planes, but most people travel by boat. You can take a big boat with a roof, or a small canoe if you prefer. Now let me tell you about some animals. The most famous fish is the piranha. Many people believe that it has big claws, but it has no claws at all. What it does have is a mouth full of very sharp teeth. Don’t worry, they rarely attack people. Another animal I love is the sloth. A cheetah moves fast, but the sloth is the opposite. It hangs in a tree and moves very slowly, so slowly that green plants grow on its fur. If you’d like to visit, think about the season. It’s wet from December until May, and the rivers rise. The best time to visit is from June to November, when you can walk on the paths and see the animals. October is hot, but a lot of people think that it’s the nicest month. Finally, a few tips. The sun is strong, even under the trees, so take a hat. An umbrella is not much use in the forest, and a coat is too warm. Bring good boots and some medicine for insect bites. And most of all, bring your curiosity. Thank you, and enjoy the Amazon!

gaps.prompt: No other river in South America goes as far as the Amazon, so it is the ___
gaps.explanation: She says that in South America no other river goes as far, so they call it the longest.

gaps.prompt: Most people get around the forest by ___
gaps.explanation: There are few roads; some use planes but most people use a boat.

gaps.prompt: A piranha has a mouth full of sharp ___
gaps.explanation: She says it has no claws, but a mouth full of sharp teeth.

gaps.prompt: Green plants grow on the fur of the sloth because it moves so ___
gaps.explanation: The sloth is the opposite of a cheetah and moves very slowly.
The best time is June to November, when the paths are dry.

gaps.prompt: Take a ___ because the sun is strong
gaps.explanation: She says take a hat; an umbrella is not much use and a coat is too warm.

parts.title: An interview with a forest guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Duarte, welcome to the programme. You have worked in the forest for twenty years. How did it all start?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: Well, you might think I read about it at school, but my school had very few books, and I never saw a film about wild animals when I was a boy. It was my grandfather. He was a guide too, and from the age of six I walked behind him on every path. He taught me the names of the trees by touch, with my eyes closed.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Tell us about a moment you remember from last week.

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: A woman from Germany started to cry on the path. I was frightened for a moment, and I thought she was scared of the dark under the trees, but she said she was fine. A big blue butterfly had landed on her hand, and she said that she had never seen anything so beautiful. It made my day.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the biggest danger for visitors?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: People expect snakes and jaguars, and of course you must be careful, but the animals avoid us. And the river is safe if you listen to the boatman. The real danger is getting lost. Everything looks the same, the paths close behind you, and one wrong turn can be a disaster. That’s why I always count my visitors.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Have you noticed any changes over the years?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: Yes, sadly. The trees are not taller, they are as old as they were. We also have more visitors than before, which is good for the villages. What worries me is the birds. There are some that my grandfather showed me, and I haven’t seen them for ten years. They have gone.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice do you give to young people who want your job?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: Don’t spend years in a university, you don’t need that. And you needn’t be fast or a good swimmer either. Be patient, because the forest shows you things only when you wait, and learn English, because most of our visitors speak it. That is the most useful thing.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you have any dreams for the future?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: I do. I won’t write a book, I’m too tired in the evenings, and I wouldn’t move to the city, I’d miss the sounds. I’d like to open a school in my village. The children now walk two hours to get to school, and many stop going. If it were close, they could learn and still help their families.

questions.prompt: How did Duarte first learn about the forest?
options: From books that he read at school
From his grandfather, who was a guide
From a film about wild animals he saw
questions.explanation: He did not read about it at school or see a film; his grandfather, a guide, taught him from the age of six.

questions.prompt: Why did a visitor cry last week?
options: She was scared of the dark
She was moved by a butterfly
questions.explanation: He thought she was scared of the dark, but she was touched by a butterfly on her hand.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest danger, according to Duarte?
questions.explanation: Animals avoid us and the river is safe; the real danger is getting lost because everything looks the same.

questions.prompt: What change has he noticed?
questions.explanation: The trees are as old as before and there are more visitors, but some birds have not been seen for ten years.

questions.prompt: What advice does he give to young people?
questions.explanation: He says do not spend years at university and you need not be fast; be patient and learn English.

questions.prompt: Why does Duarte want to open a school?
options: He enjoyed school as a boy
questions.explanation: He does not want to write a book or move to the city; the children walk two hours to school and many stop going.
